name: Set Theory
description: A lens for composing Factors from the language of extensional collections, transfinite hierarchies, and forcing extensions. Maps set-theoretic concepts—sets, classes, ordinals, cardinals, the cumulative hierarchy, and forcing—to the 19-node topology. Useful for Factors involving collections, hierarchies, partial knowledge, and the foundations of mathematics.

x.note: The depth anchor—every nonempty set has an ∈‑minimal element. Part of the 4‑cycle x→a→9→y→x, linking well‑foundedness to the empty set, forcing relation, and extensionality.

y.note: The relational anchor—sets are determined by their elements. Part of the 4‑cycle x→a→9→y→x, tying extensionality to well‑foundedness, the empty set, and forcing relation.

z.note: The transformational anchor—no infinite descending ∈‑chains. Persistently connected to 0 (observer/condition), reflecting that the axiom of foundation grounds the observer’s construction.

0.note: When present, represents a partial condition in a forcing extension. Persistently connected to z (foundation), linking the observer’s state to the well‑foundedness of the universe.

1.note: A set as a bounded collection. Part of the 4‑cycle 1→6→5→2→1, connecting sets to transitive closure, definable collections, and elements.

2.note: Primitive members of a set. Completes the 1‑6‑5‑2 cycle, showing how elements are embedded in sets, transitive closure, and definable collections.

3.note: The invariant laws—extensionality, foundation, replacement, choice, etc. A node in the 7‑core; connected to choice function (c) and forcing poset (e), as axioms include choice and forcing adds sets that respect the axioms.

4.note: The fundamental relation connecting elements to sets. A node in the 7‑core; connected to generic filter (b) and closure (f), as membership is the basis for forcing and the closure of the universe.

5.note: Patterns definable by formulas. Part of the 1‑6‑5‑2 cycle, bridging transitive closure and elements.

6.note: The transformation that closes a set under membership. Part of the 1‑6‑5‑2 cycle, connecting sets to definable collections.

7.note: Actualized stage in the cumulative hierarchy. Persistently connected to 8 (power set), linking the stage to the operation that generates higher ranks.

8.note: The operation that generates granularity. Persistently connected to 7 (V_α), reflecting that each stage is the power set of the previous limit.

9.note: The event where a condition forces a statement. Part of the 4‑cycle x→a→9→y→x, placing the forcing relation between well‑foundedness, the empty set, and extensionality.

a.note: Pure potential—the set with no members. Initiates the 4‑cycle x→a→9→y→x, linking the empty set to well‑foundedness, forcing, and extensionality.

b.note: The unpredictable selection that resolves undetermined truth. A node in the 7‑core; connected to membership (4) and transitive model (d), as the generic filter adds new sets to the transitive model.

c.note: Directional bias—a function selecting distinguished elements. A node in the 7‑core; connected to ZFC axioms (3) and transitive model (d), as choice is part of ZFC and holds in transitive models.

d.note: Persistent structure—models like L, HOD, or V[G]. A node in the 7‑core; connected to generic filter (b), choice function (c), and closure (f), as transitive models contain generic filters and respect choice.

e.note: The active algorithm—a partial order of conditions. A node in the 7‑core; connected to ZFC axioms (3) and closure (f), as the poset is defined in ZFC and determines the generic extension.

f.note: The resonant cavity—the completed universe. A node in the 7‑core; connected to membership (4), transitive model (d), and forcing poset (e), forming the central hub of the set‑theoretic universe.

n.formula: n = rank level (α such that V_α is considered)

m.formula: m = log₂(κ) where κ is the cardinality of the power set of some set, or the number of elements in a finite set

phase.formula: φ(p) = { q ≤ p | q ⊩ ψ } / dense sets
phase.special: May be given as interval or partial order when uncertain
phase.significance: Phase encodes the truth value of a statement relative to a condition in a forcing poset.

cumulative.description: The Factor viewed as a stage in the cumulative hierarchy V_α
cumulative.phase_condition: Phases increase with rank—each power set operation adds π/19

forcing.description: The Factor viewed as a condition in a partial order, awaiting generic extension
forcing.phase_condition: Phase is partial—the Factor's truth value is not yet determined

class.description: The Factor viewed as a proper class—too large to be a set, closure is a limit condition
class.phase_condition: No closure—f is absent; phases approach a limit ordinal

creating_anew.note: When creating a set-theoretic structure, start with the empty set (node a), build up via power set (node 8) and union, and use the cumulative hierarchy (node 7) to track rank.

translating_known.forcing_extension: Map to nodes a-b-e (Ocean/Chaos/Factor) — conditions, generic filter, poset
translating_known.proper_class: f absent — closure is a limit condition, not a current state

temporary_note.special: f may be omitted or marked as 'pending'. The Factor is a condition in a forcing poset—awaiting generic extension.

constraints.well_foundedness: Node x ensures every nonempty set has an ∈‑minimal element.
constraints.extensionality: Node y ensures sets are uniquely determined by their elements.
constraints.power_set_operation: Node 8 (power set) must produce a set of strictly larger cardinality (Cantor's theorem).
constraints.forcing_closure: When using forcing, node f may be omitted or marked pending; the Factor is an incomplete condition.
constraints.stratum_preference: global for general set theory; trefoil_g for forcing extensions (transformative); fig8 for wild or non‑well‑founded set theories
constraints.invariant_core: The Set Theory paradigm respects the persistent skeleton from trefoil_i, which decomposes into five subsystems: (1) edge 0→z linking observer/condition to foundation, (2) edge 8→7 linking power set to V_α stage, (3) 4‑cycle x→a→9→y→x linking well‑foundedness–empty set–forcing relation–extensionality, (4) 4‑cycle 1→6→5→2→1 linking set–transitive closure–definable collection–element, and (5) 7‑node core {3,4,b,c,d,e,f} encoding the heart of set theory: ZFC axioms–membership–generic filter–choice function–transitive model–forcing poset–closure.
